Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn these notes into a one-page triage card for volunteers at the saturday repair cafe? keep it plain language and easy to scan, maybe use a heading for check-in and one for safety. At check-in, record the owner's name, best contact, item, and what is going wrong. For an electrical item, look for exposed wiring, a swollen battery, or a part that feels hot. If any of those signs are present, don't plug it in or test it; put it on the marked hold shelf and tell the shift coordinator. If an electrical item has none of those signs, continue with normal intake, but don't do a powered test unless the owner gives permission. For an item that isn't electrical, use normal intake and ask the owner before doing any test. Please make the difference between the warning-sign branch and the other branch clear, and don't make it sound like volunteers should diagnose or repair a hazardous item. Keep the card focused on these check-in and triage steps; it isn't meant to explain how to repair anything.", "output": "Draft a one-page, plain-language triage card for volunteers at the Saturday repair cafe. Make it easy to scan, with headings for check-in and safety.

At check-in, volunteers should record the owner's name, best contact, item, and what is going wrong.

For electrical items:
- If the item has exposed wiring, a swollen battery, or a part that feels hot, do not plug it in or test it. Put it on the marked hold shelf and tell the shift coordinator.
- If none of those warning signs are present, continue with normal intake. Do not do a powered test unless the owner gives permission.

For items that are not electrical, use normal intake and ask the owner before doing any test. Make the difference between the warning-sign branch and the other branch clear. Do not suggest that volunteers should diagnose or repair a hazardous item. Keep the card focused on check-in and triage; do not explain how to repair anything."}]
